name: Goulash Communism
scope: The Hungarian one-party socialist system under János Kádár after the 1956 revolution (consolidated from the early 1960s; the 1968 New Economic Mechanism is its centrepiece), which the defining sources call 'goulash communism' (Győri, Bozóki, Nyyssönen, Benczes) or goulash/fridge-socialism (Halmesvirta). They present it as a 'nondemocratic yet liveable' deviation from Rákosi-era Stalinism and orthodox Marxism-Leninism: Soviet loyalty in foreign affairs, one-party rule and secret-police surveillance, traded for rising living standards, a paternalist welfare state, consumer goods, limited market mechanisms and a depoliticised private sphere ('who is not against us is with us'). It excludes the Rákosi era and Soviet-bloc communism in general. Kádár's own 1956 appeal is taken as the regime's founding text because Kádár is its key figure.

summary: A one-party socialist system under János Kádár that, after 1956 and especially after the 1968 New Economic Mechanism, kept Soviet alignment and the party's political monopoly while trading limited economic decentralisation, consumer goods and a paternalist welfare state for political quiet ('whoever is not against us is with us').
